Interface IuOidcClientConfiguration

public interface IuOidcClientConfiguration
Describes one relying party registered with this provider.

A client is registered on its own rather than as an entry inside the provider's configuration, so registering or revoking one is a change scoped to that client alone. Having nothing to read for a client_id is how an unregistered client is refused.

Property names use lower case with underscores, so getClientId() reads client_id.

    • getClientId

      String getClientId()
      Gets the client ID, which is also the key this registration is read by.
      Returns:
      Client ID

    • isEnabled

      boolean isEnabled()
      Determines whether this client may be used.

      A disabled client stays registered but is refused, so taking one out of service doesn't discard the endpoints, keys, and resources it was registered with, and restoring it doesn't mean registering it again.

      Returns:
      true if the client may be used; false to refuse it as if it were unregistered

    • getAdminRoles

      Iterable<String> getAdminRoles()
      Gets the identity roles that entitle an end user to administer this client's own registration.

      These govern who may change what this registration describes, not what the client may do once registered; a request through the client is governed by the endpoint it names. Holding any one of them is enough.

      Returns:
      identity role names; null or empty to admit no one

    • getEndpoints

      Iterable<IuOidcClientEndpoint> getEndpoints()
      Gets the endpoints this client is registered for, one per redirect URI.

      The requested redirect_uri selects one, and only that endpoint's resources bear on what the request may ask for.

      Returns:
      registered endpoints

    • getRoles

      Iterable<IuOidcClientRole> getRoles()
      Iterates roles mapped for this client.
      Returns:
      mapped roles

    • getUserinfoAlg

      default edu.iu.crypt.WebKey.Algorithm getUserinfoAlg()
      Gets the algorithm a UserInfo response to this client is signed with.

      Registered for the client rather than for one of its endpoints, unlike the algorithm an ID token is signed with, because a UserInfo request names no endpoint: it presents an access token, and a token names the client it was issued to and not the redirect URI the grant behind it went through. There is nothing at that point to select an endpoint by.

      Also unlike an ID token, which is always signed: null is the default and means the response is a plain claims document, which is what OpenID Connect means by registering no signing algorithm.

      Returns:
      signature WebKey.Algorithm; null (default) to answer an unsigned document

    • getUserinfoEnc

      default edu.iu.crypt.WebEncryption.Encryption getUserinfoEnc()
      Gets the content encryption algorithm a UserInfo response to this client is encrypted with.

      Independent of getUserinfoAlg(). Registering encryption alone answers an encrypted claims document, which is confidential but unauthenticated; registering both answers a signature encrypted to the client's key, which is both.

      Returns:
      WebEncryption.Encryption; null (default) to answer an unencrypted document

    • getUserinfoJwk

      default edu.iu.crypt.WebKey getUserinfoJwk()
      Gets the key a UserInfo response to this client is encrypted to.

      Required when getUserinfoEnc() names an encryption, and unread otherwise. Registered for the client for the same reason the algorithms are.

      Returns:
      encryption WebKey; null (default) when nothing is encrypted to this client
